rv.q: You can't travel through the arboreal forests surrounding Spamalot without a smile on your face and a few belly laughs deeper down.
What I can say is that I think I enjoyed this production more.

The roaring laughter, hoots, and whistles from the audience throughout the play, culminating in multiple curtain calls, confirmed that they were not disappointed and truly appreciated the spectacular performances they just witnessed.
Before these valiant (and silly) knights once more depart to far-off (and sillier) lands, you must make it your quest to see this fabulously (silly) show while still in Massachusetts.
There’s a level of energy and dedication to the work that makes it the kind of evening full of laughter and frivolity that Twin Cities residents could really use right now.
Spamalot mostly succeeds at delivering barbs with bouquets.
You will likely still laugh loudly, and it doesn’t take a decree from a king or an enchanted prophesy from a lake to make that happen.
Did I still leave smiling at the show’s utter silliness? Absolutely.
For individuals looking to escape and laugh a little, or to drag their grandkids to a very confusing night of musical theater, Spamalot is the perfect show for you.

cn.t: Critics enthusiastically embrace this touring production of "Spamalot," praising its inspired silliness, joyful absurdity, and crowd-pleasing humor that delivers exactly the laugh-out-loud escapism audiences crave.
